observations: Compact photo printer with a tilting LCD screen.
Branding 'Canon' and 'SELPHY CP1000' visible on the top panel.
The LCD screen surface shows heavy bubbling or peeling, possibly a protective film or damage to the polarizer.
Control panel features buttons for Power, Menu, Edit, OK, Back, and Print.
Front slots for CF/microdrive and SD memory cards are visible.
A paper cassette is attached in photo 1.
The body shows some surface scuffs and dust.

claims.evidence: Photo 1 and 2 show significant bubbling/deterioration on the screen surface and visible scuffs on the casing.
Photo 1 and 2 show the model name SELPHY CP1000.
The SELPHY CP series is designed specifically for 4x6 inch (postcard size) thermal dye-sublimation printing.

risks.risk: The LCD screen may be permanently damaged or unreadable.
risks.proof: A photo of the device powered on showing a clear menu on the screen.

risks.risk: The internal printing mechanism or thermal head may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video of the device successfully printing a test photo.

risks.risk: The proprietary power adapter (CA-CP200) may be missing.
risks.proof: A photo of the power brick and cable.

proof_requests: A photo of the printer powered on with the screen active.
A video of the printer completing a full print cycle.
A photo of the power adapter and any included ink/paper supplies.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as a Canon Selphy CP1000. Due to the poor condition of the screen and lack of power-on proof, it must be priced at its lowest value as a non-functional or parts-only unit.
